$comment: Which sunrise cities get phase 2's prose passage and which are held back as a
control. Recorded BEFORE shipping, because an assignment reconstructed afterwards
1. The nine cities with measurable GSC impressions are assigned greedily — each in
descending order goes to whichever group currently has the smaller total. That
lands at 1914 vs 1945 impressions, a 1.6% gap, which pairwise splitting could not
reach because Madrid alone is a quarter of the volume.
2. The other 31 have no measurable volume and alternate in SUNRISE_CITIES order — a
stable ordering that predates this experiment and was not chosen for it.
MEASUREMENT LIMIT, so the pairing is not read as more precise than it is: Search
Console's page table virtualises and would not render past 10 rows, so only those
nine cities have real numbers. The other 31 are each below 39 impressions in 90 days
— the lowest measured value — and are treated as equivalent. That is enough: the
split only has to balance where there is volume to balance.

readOut.$comment: Written before the data arrives, so the reading is not chosen to fit whatever happens.
readOut.bothMove: Something other than the passage caused it — an algorithm update, phase 1 landing, or seasonality. The passage is not shown to work.
readOut.treatedOnly: The passage is the lever. Ship it to the control group immediately.
readOut.neitherMoves: The passage is not the lever. Next candidate is authority, which is untouched and known to bind crawl.
readOut.controlOnly: Something is wrong with the measurement or the split. Investigate before concluding anything.
readOut.deadline: If the treated group has not moved 12 weeks after Google has recrawled it, ship the control group anyway. The experiment does not get to outlive its usefulness.
